newsitem.title: USA: Minn. House panel facing Twins stadium deadline.
newsitem.headline: Minn. House panel facing Twins stadium deadline.

text.p: A Minnesota House committee must meet a midnight Wednesday deadline to move legislation for a new Minnesota Twins stadium or the effort will likely die, a spokesman for the committee chairwoman said Tuesday.

The House Local Government and Metropolitan Affairs Committee voted against advancing the proposal last week and was expected to consider a modified version of the proposal late Wednesday, said Bob DeBoer, spokesman for Rep. Ann Rest, D-New Hope.

Rest, the chief sponsor, only seeks to advance the proposal to the House tax committee without a recommendation, DeBoer said. Other controversial bills have been advanced for consideration by the entire House, he added.

The modified bill would seek to better define the boundaries for a downtown special economic development district, DeBoer said. Committee members cited concerns about the boundaries when voting 10-9 not to advance the proposal last week, he noted.
The proposed economic development district would include a portion of downtown Minneapolis, not the entire city center, DeBoer said. Addressing that one concern could change a vote, he said.

A Senate committee earlier stripped public financing from a companion bill before advancing that proposal. Rest has no plans to strip the financing recommendations from the House version, DeBoer said.
Without a companion in the House, it "would be extremely difficult for a Senate bill to come over," DeBoer said.
Early estimates pegged the cost of a new stadium at from $250 million to $300 million or more if a retractable roof is added.
